cues.text: Before we start, Spiros and Hiroko, thanks for coming in today to talk about your recent study experiences and congratulations to you both in doing so well in your first semester exams!
cues.speaker: TEACHER

cues.text: I'd like to discuss with you the value of the English for Academic Purposes course you did here last year before starting your university course.
cues.speaker: TEACHER

cues.text: Spiros, if I could start with you,what parts of the programme have now proved to be particularly valuable to you?
cues.speaker: TEACHER

cues.text: I think that having to do a seminar presentation really helped me, For example, a couple of weeks ago in our marketing subject, when it was my turn to give a presentation I felt quite confident.
cues.speaker: SPIROS

cues.text: Of course, I was still nervous but because i had done one before, I knew what to expect.
cues.speaker: SPIROS

cues.text: Alse, I know I was well-prepared and I had practised my timing.
cues.speaker: SPIROS

cues.text: In fact, I think that in relation to some of the other people in my group, I did quite a good job because my overall style was quite professional.
cues.speaker: SPIROS

cues.text: What about you, Hiroko?
cues.speaker: SPIROS

cues.text: Mmm, that's interesting.
cues.speaker: HIROKO

cues.text: In my group, I was really surprised by the way the students did their presentations - they just read their ontes aloud!
cues.speaker: HIROKO

cues.text: Can you believe that?
cues.speaker: HIROKO

cues.text: They didn't worry about their presentation style or keeping eye contact with their audience - and I remember that these things were really stressed to us in the course here.
cues.speaker: HIROKO

cues.text: So, how did you approach your presentation, Hiroko?
cues.speaker: TEACHER

cues.text: Well, to speak frankly, I read my notes too!
cues.speaker: HIROKO

cues.text: At the time, it was a relief to do it this way, but actually when I had finished, I didn't feel any real sense of satisfaction.
cues.speaker: HIROKO

cues.text: I didn't feel positive about the experience at all.
cues.speaker: HIROKO

cues.text: That's a pity.
cues.speaker: SPIROS

cues.text: You know, although I was pleased with my presentation, I am not so pleased with my actual performance right now in the tutorials - during the whole semester, I've not said anything in our tutorial discussions.
cues.speaker: SPIROS

cues.text: Not a word.
cues.speaker: SPIROS

cues.text: Really, Spiros?
cues.speaker: HIROKO

cues.text: Why's that?
cues.speaker: HIROKO

cues.text: Do the other students talk too much?
cues.speaker: HIROKO

cues.text: It's partly that, but it's mostly because I have had no confidence to speak out.
cues.speaker: SPIROS

cues.text: Their style of speaking is so different - it's not the style we were used to during the course.
cues.speaker: SPIROS

cues.text: They use so many colloquialisms, they're not very polite and sometimes there seems to be no order in their discussion.
cues.speaker: SPIROS

cues.text: Also, they are very familiar with each other, so because they know each other's habits, they can let each other into the discussion.
cues.speaker: SPIROS

cues.text: You're right, Spiros, I've experienced that too.
cues.speaker: HIROKO

cues.text: For most of this semester, I've said absolutely nothing in tutorials.
cues.speaker: HIROKO

cues.text: But recently, I've been trying to speak up more and I just jump in, and I've noticed an interesting thing.
cues.speaker: HIROKO

cues.text: I've noticed that if they thought my point was interesting or new, then the next time they actually asked for my opinion, and then it was much easier for me to be part of the discussion.
cues.speaker: HIROKO

cues.text: That's great, Hiroko!
cues.speaker: SPIROS

cues.text: I hope that happens for me next semester - I'll have to work hard to find some interesting points.
cues.speaker: SPIROS

cues.text: What helped you to find these ideas?
cues.speaker: SPIROS

cues.text: I think that one thing that helped me with this was the reading.
cues.speaker: HIROKO

cues.text: I've had to do so much reading this semester just to help me make sense of the lectures.
cues.speaker: HIROKO

cues.text: At first I couldn't understand what the lecturers were talking about, so I had to turn to the books and journals.
cues.speaker: HIROKO

cues.text: Every night I read for hours, using the lists of references that were given, and I made pages of notes.
cues.speaker: HIROKO

cues.text: At breakfast, I read and read my notes again.
cues.speaker: HIROKO

cues.text: This habit has helped me to follow the ideas in the lectures, and it's also given me some ideas to use in the tutorials.
cues.speaker: HIROKO

cues.text: But i did so much reading anyway - I don't think there's any time left over for anything extra.
cues.speaker: SPIROS

cues.text: My reading speed is still quite slow, though I'm much better at dealing with vocabulary than I used to be.
cues.speaker: SPIROS

cues.text: What else do you think we could add to the course program to help with this reading problem?
cues.speaker: TEACHER

cues.text: There's not really anything because it's my problem.
cues.speaker: SPIROS

cues.text: I remember we were given long articles to read.
cues.speaker: SPIROS

cues.text: We didn't like that but now I realise that reading those long articleswas good preparation for the things I need to read now.
cues.speaker: SPIROS

cues.text: Also, in class we regularly had speed-reading tasks to do, and we kept a record of our reading speed, so the teachers were encouraging us to work on that.
cues.speaker: SPIROS

cues.text: That's true Spiros, but what we read could have been different.
cues.speaker: HIROKO

cues.text: Sometimes in the English class I felt frustrated when I had to read articles about the environment or health or education, because I wanted to concentrate on my own field, but we didn't read anything about engineering.
cues.speaker: HIROKO

cues.text: So, I think I wasted some time learning vocabulary didn't need.
cues.speaker: HIROKO

cues.text: But surely the strategies you were taught for dealing with that vocabulary were helpful.
cues.speaker: TEACHER

cues.text: Yes, but psychologically speaking, I would have felt much better working on reading from my own field.
cues.speaker: HIROKO

cues.text: What do you think Spiros?
cues.speaker: HIROKO

cues.text: I agree, that would have helped my confidence too and I would have been more motivated.
cues.speaker: SPIROS

cues.text: It was good though that we could work on our own topics when we wrote the research assignments.
cues.speaker: SPIROS

cues.text: Okay, let's move on to writing now ...
cues.speaker: TEACHER
